# Nicholas Anakwue

> Digital Politics & Social Movements Researcher | PhD Candidate at Queen Mary University of London

## About Me
I am a computational social sciences and African digital politics researcher. My work sits at the intersection of digital politics, technology governance, and product strategy. I am currently an ESRC-funded PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London, and a recipient of the 2023 LISS DTP Studentship and International Doctoral Scholar Award. 

Before academia, I spent years designing and executing growth strategies for African tech startups in civic-tech/gov-tech, media, and e-commerce, and writing investment memos for seed-stage ventures. I am a DreamVC LIVC Fellow and a former Venture Partner at Republic.

## Research Focus & Methodology
I analyze large-scale social networks to understand how protest movements in Africa (particularly in Nigeria and Zimbabwe, such as #EndSARS and #ThisFlag) mobilize collective political identity through digital platforms. 

My theoretical contribution extends connective action theory through the lens of network architecture to a "logic of collection," showing how the structural shapes of digital conversation either concentrate or distribute political agency in social movements.

**Methodologies used:**
* Exponential Random Graph Models (ERGM)
* Dynamic Network Actor Models (DyNAM)
* Large-scale social network analysis
* In-depth qualitative interviews
* Extensive localized fieldwork
